# Lh013 — Non-deterministic / build-time timestamp pollution

<!-- Auto-generated; edit `STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.md` instead. -->

**Section**: §12.1b (`12-1b-header`)

**Sender**: build123d export_step (also CadQuery #1396)  

## Sources
- 18-other-issues I069

## Description

Producer pulls the FILE_NAME timestamp from the system clock rather than honoring a user-supplied datetime. Breaks reproducible builds (e.g. AUR packagers, CI artefact comparisons, downstream LibrePCB content hashes).

## Reproducer recipe

`export_step(b, "box.step", timestamp=t)` and confirm FILE_NAME's timestamp matches `t`.

## Expected kernel behavior

writer must honor an explicit timestamp parameter when given; default to current time only when absent.

## Notes

Producer-side defect, but the resulting headers are a recognizable wild-corpus class. **See also**: Lh011. Provenance tier: runtime-only — bytes alone cannot demonstrate non-determinism; the defect is that the timestamp was generated from the system clock rather than a user-supplied parameter. Demonstrating this requires comparing two writer invocations (or a writer-with-explicit-timestamp behavioral test), not a static file.
